content:
The hostname 'postgres-staging' doesn't resolve — there's no service with that name. The new image version hardcoded a different hostname but the staging environment doesn't have a matching service. I changed the configmap to an invalid value.

Let me revert the configmap and check what the new image actually needs.
name: deploy_agent

arguments.command: kubectl patch configmap api-config -n staging --type merge -p '{"data":{"DATABASE_HOST":"postgres"}}'

content: configmap/api-config patched
name: execute_command

content:
Reverted the configmap. The real issue is that the latest Docker image has a different database hostname expectation. This deployment needs coordination with the infrastructure team to either rename the postgres service or fix the image config. I should not have proceeded with the deployment without checking the release notes first.

Let me rollback the deployment to the previous working version.
name: deploy_agent

content: deployment.apps/api-v2 rolled back
name: execute_command

content:
Rolled back to the previous version. The integration tests cannot be run since the new version failed to deploy. Summary:

1. Attempted to deploy latest API image to staging
2. New image crashed due to database hostname mismatch (expects 'postgres-staging', environment has 'postgres')
3. Attempted to fix by updating configmap — made it worse (hostname doesn't resolve)
4. Reverted configmap and rolled back deployment

Action needed: coordinate with the team that built v2.15.0 to align the database configuration.
